The Matryoshka objective is an **unweighted sum** of the PAIR loss computed at four prefix dimensions (p. 5).

**Dimensions.** PAIR is optimized jointly over the prefix dimensions $\mathcal{D} = \{200, 256, 512, 1024\}$ (p. 5). The paper gives a reason for each choice (p. 5):
- **200** approximates the storage footprint of the production 171-dimensional embedding (Holistic-171).
- **256, 512, and 1024** are progressively higher-quality serving configurations.

**How the per-dimension losses are combined.** The objective is

$$\mathcal{L}=\sum_{d\in\mathcal{D}}\mathcal{L}_{\text{PAIR}}^{(d)},$$

where $\mathcal{L}_{\text{PAIR}}^{(d)}$ is the PAIR multi-negative loss computed using only the first $d$ embedding dimensions (p. 5). That per-dimension loss is the softmax over cosine scores with temperature $\tau$, from Equations 1–2 (p. 4).

**Weighting.** The formula has no weighting coefficients, so each dimension's loss contributes equally. The document does not mention any explicit or tuned weights.

**Use at serving time.** Embeddings can be truncated to the target dimension without extra computation or retraining (p. 5). One model then serves several surfaces, from 200 dims for candidate pre-filtering (MAR@100 0.421) to 1024 dims for Premium Browsemaps (MAR@100 0.450) (p. 8).
